# Disagreement Log — Proto-Gospel of James Chapter 16

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Agents:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Chapter:** POX 16 — The ordeal of the bitter water; both acquitted

---

## Disagreements

**1. 16:1 — "water of the conviction of the Lord"**
- EMET: "water of the conviction of the Lord"
- LOGOS: "water of the Lord's conviction"
- PNEUMA: "water of testing — the water of divine conviction"
- Note: Greek *hydōr elegmou Kyriou* = "water of the Lord's testing/conviction/refutation." PNEUMA adds "water of testing" as a doublet, which is not in the Greek. EMET preserves "conviction" as an accurate legal-theological term.

**2. 16:1 — "make your sin manifest before your eyes"**
- EMET: "make your sin manifest before your eyes"
- LOGOS: "reveal your sin to your own eyes"
- PNEUMA: "If there is sin in you, it will show itself"
- Note: Greek *dēlōsei tēn hamartian sou emprosthen tōn ophthalmōn sou* = "will make manifest your sin before your eyes." EMET is most literal; PNEUMA weakens the directness.

**3. 16:2 — "made Joseph drink" / "sent him into the wilderness"**
- EMET: "made Joseph drink and sent him into the wilderness"
- LOGOS: "gave it to Joseph to drink, then sent him out into the wilderness"
- PNEUMA: "sent out into the hill country"
- Note: PNEUMA's "hill country" (*eis to oros*) may reflect a different MS reading. Greek generally has "wilderness" (*erēmos*) or "the hill country."

**4. 16:2 — "came back whole"**
- EMET: "came back whole" (twice, as a refrain)
- LOGOS: "returned unharmed" (twice)
- PNEUMA: "came back completely unharmed" / "came back unharmed too"
- Note: Greek *hygeias* = "healthy/whole." EMET's "whole" preserves the biblical wholeness vocabulary (cf. Luke 17:19 *hygiēs*). LOGOS/PNEUMA's "unharmed" are accurate but miss the positive "wholeness" sense.

**5. 16:2 — "all the people marveled"**
- EMET: "all the people marveled because sin was not revealed in them"
- LOGOS: "All the people were astonished"
- PNEUMA: "The crowd that had gathered watched in amazement"
- Note: PNEUMA adds "that had gathered" — not in the Greek. Greek *ho laos* = "the people."

**6. 16:3 — "neither do I condemn you"**
- EMET: "neither do I condemn you"
- LOGOS/PNEUMA: "neither shall I / will I not condemn you"
- Note: The priest's formula deliberately echoes John 8:11 ("Neither do I condemn you"). All three renderings capture this; EMET is closest to the Johannine phrasing.
